post_title: By how many percentage points will Okta (OKTA) outperform or underperform the software ETF IGV between the October 30 and November 13, 2026 market closes?

question.title: By how many percentage points will Okta (OKTA) outperform or underperform the software ETF IGV between the October 30 and November 13, 2026 market closes?
question.description:
Okta, Inc. (Nasdaq: OKTA) is a US identity and access management company whose single sign-on (SSO) and multi-factor authentication products are widely used by enterprises and governments, including the US Department of Homeland Security. On October 28, 2026, the leak-publishing site Distributed Denial of Secrets released records on more than 41,000 current and former DHS employees and contractors — including names, work addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, managers and job descriptions, with ICE and CBP agents among those affected (roughly 15% of DHS's 260,000+ workforce).

A group calling itself "Department of Peace" claimed it harvested the data from the Okta SSO service DHS uses to reach its central environment, citing opposition to immigration enforcement; Reuters could not immediately corroborate the claim. DHS told employees on October 29 that it was aware of a "potential breach" and was working to address it, and reporting noted that a DHS Okta environment would also hold IT and log-in records, including which internal systems and applications individual employees can access. Publicly, Okta's only on-record response so far is a blanket denial given to reporters: "Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised." Okta's next scheduled disclosure event, its Q3 FY2027 earnings call, is expected around December 1–2, 2026 — after this question resolves.

Okta has been the vector of high-profile intrusions before (LAPSUS$ in 2022; the October 2023 support-case-management breach), and its shares have historically sold off on such disclosures. Recent closes: $222.66 on October 28 (the day the leak was published), $221.86 on October 29, and $208.24 on October 30, when the stock fell about 6% after trading as high as $222.40 — a move that came amid a broad software selloff (Fortinet's guidance cut, ServiceNow's steepest one-day drop, Nasdaq −2.86%), not on DHS-specific news. Earlier in October the shares fell roughly 10% in a single session during an AI-linked rotation before recovering; OKTA is up more than 100% year to date. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV), a widely used benchmark for US enterprise-software stocks, closed at $104.29 on October 30, 2026.

Because both stocks move with software-sector sentiment, this question measures Okta's return relative to IGV over the two weeks to Friday, November 13, 2026 — i.e. whether investors end up pricing in Okta-specific damage from the DHS incident, or treat it as noise. A negative value means Okta underperformed the software sector.

question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves from Okta's (ticker OKTA) return minus the return of the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (ticker IGV) over the period from the October 30, 2026 regular-session close to the November 13, 2026 regular-session close, expressed in percentage points. Both returns are computed from the "Close" column of the daily historical tables at https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/OKTA/history/ and https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/IGV/history/.

Value = [100 × (OKTA close on Nov 13, 2026 ÷ OKTA close on Oct 30, 2026)] − [100 × (IGV close on Nov 13, 2026 ÷ IGV close on Oct 30, 2026)], i.e. OKTA's percent change minus IGV's percent change. For example, if OKTA rises 5% and IGV rises 2% over the period, the question resolves as 3; if OKTA falls 4% while IGV rises 1%, it resolves as -5.

If either table has no November 13, 2026 row (for example because the exchange was closed for the whole session), the most recent session before November 14, 2026 that appears in both tables is used for both tickers. If the Yahoo Finance pages are unavailable, the corresponding "Close" values at https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/okta/history/ and https://stockanalysis.com/etf/igv/history/ are used; if both sites are unavailable, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
question.fine_print: Only regular-session closing prices from the two tables are used; pre-market, after-hours and "Adj Close" values do not count. Both legs must be computed over the same pair of sessions.
